transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Tell me about a time you saw a problem that wasn't yours to fix, and you fixed it anyway.

transcript.speaker: candidate
transcript.text: We had an issue with our staging environment failing every Friday. The infra team was supposed to handle it. I saw some logs but didn't dig in because it wasn't my area. They fixed it eventually.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Tell me about a time you disagreed with a teammate on a technical decision.

transcript.speaker: candidate
transcript.text: My teammate wanted to use GraphQL and I preferred REST. We discussed it briefly but our manager made the final call. We went with GraphQL. It wasn't a big deal to me either way.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Tell me about a time you were wrong about something technical.

transcript.speaker: candidate
transcript.text: I was wrong about how React's rendering batching worked before version 18. I had written code that assumed state updates were always batched. I refactored the components once I understood the actual behavior.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Tell me about a time you had to push back on a direction you disagreed with.

transcript.speaker: candidate
transcript.text: We were asked to skip QA on a release. I said I wasn't comfortable with that and sent a note to my lead. He agreed and we did a shortened QA pass instead. It was a small push-back.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: What's a weakness you've had to actively work on?

transcript.speaker: candidate
transcript.text: I've gotten feedback that my written communication is too terse. I've been adding more context in Slack and PRs. I think it's improved but I'm not sure by how much.
